title: Introduce scenario-driven workload choreographer and unified profile shaper
author: Aisha Khatri
release_notes: Adds a scenario choreographer and profile shaper used by benchmark-lab to synthesize representative warmup sequences and merge histogram outputs into compact delta baselines. No user-facing API changes.
description: Context: benchmark runs have drifted between synthetic micro-runners and customer traces; we need a lightweight orchestration layer that composes small representative workload fragments into realistic end-to-end scenarios and a compact profiling shaper that synthesizes warmup sequences from trace signatures. Motivation: existing runners either replay full sessions (heavy, brittle) or emit tiny microbenchmarks (fast but unrepresentative). This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: (1) Scenario Choreographer - a declarative DSL and runtime that stitches together mix fragments (short priming bursts, sustained background queries, tail events) with tunable phase timings and probabilistic branching so we can express real-world mixes with a small number of scenarios; (2) Unified Profile Shaper - a trace-signature extractor and warmup synthesizer that converts aggregated KV-cache/sequence histograms into an efficient primer sequence and outputs a canonical histogram-merger artifact so downstream reporters can compute delta baselines. Changes in this PR: - New CLI: benchctl scenario apply/plan/exec with flags --seed/--duration/--kv-policy; examples in docs/scenario/README.md. - Scenario DSL: yaml-based, supports phases, branch weights, sequenced priming, and named fragments. - Profile shaper: profiler/shape.py that reads trace signatures (token-length and kv-hit distributions) and emits primer packs. - Histogram merger: telemetry/merge_histograms.go consolidates per-run histograms into compact delta baselines and supports configurable bucketing strategies. - Reporting pipeline: integrates merger output into existing reporters so nightly jobs produce per-scenario delta baselines and a smoothed p95 trend. How it was tested: unit tests for DSL parsing and shape synthesis, integration runs in the perf-canary cluster with 3 representative scenarios, and end-to-end nightly pipeline run on a trimmed dataset. Results: on the mixed-dialog scenario the new primer pack reduced cold-start p95 by ~18% and decreased the number of warmup tokens required by ~42% vs naive replay. The histogram-merger reduced storage footprint of baseline artifacts by ~60% through delta-encoding and adaptive bucketing. Backwards compatibility: scenario DSL is additive; existing runners still work. Migration: nightly jobs automatically pick up merged baselines; ops can opt-in per-commit via benchctl. Checklist: - [x] DSL design doc uploaded (ENG-7321) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] updated quickstart and examples - [x] performance numbers recorded and uploaded to /reports/scenario-choreographer/ - [x] add CI gating for new telemetry checks Usage examples: benchctl scenario plan examples/mixes/mixed-dialog.yaml --seed=42 benchctl scenario exec --profile merged-baseline-2024-11-01 --duration=10m Known limitations and follow-ups: the current shape synthesizer assumes stationary kv-hit distributions within a phase; we will iterate to support multi-modal phases (ENG-7340). Also plan to add adaptive primer sizing in a follow-up PR.
commit_summary: Add profile shaper (shape.py) and histogram merger (merge_histograms.go)
Integration: wire scenario outputs into nightly reporters
Fix: tighten histogram bucketing and add determinism in primer generation
review_comments: Tomás Rivera: Can the DSL express probabilistic branching between background and foreground phases? If not, please add — this is needed to model bursty user traffic.
Aisha: Yes — the DSL includes 'branches' with weights and a 'phase_rate' field. Added examples in examples/mixes/ and unit tests.
Claire Nguyen: The histogram-merger needs deterministic bucket boundaries to make nightly diffs stable. Suggest using a seeded adaptive algorithm and emit boundaries as metadata.
Aisha: Implemented deterministic bucketing using a seed derived from scenario name+date; merger emits bucket map JSON and regression tests verify stability.
Benji Patel: CI shows flakiness in the integration run on arm64 nodes (OOM when primer size is high). Can we cap primer size by default?
Aisha: Added --kv-policy=cap(512k) default and a config knob in benchctl. Also added a smoke test for arm64 in CI matrix.
Tomás: Approve after squashing remaining minor nit on log level phrasing.
Aisha: Addressed nits and squashed commits for merge.
